label: TEST-LOOP-ONLY: a teleost design's bulk density is at most a million times water
statement_en: For a teleost design that commits a standard length and a mass, mass_kg is at most 1e6 kg/m^3 times SL_m^3: the bulk density implied by the committed numbers is at most a million times that of water.

hypotheses.name: test-loop-only-density-sanity#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: the committed SL_m is a length of the same body the committed mass_kg weighs, and the body's volume is at least SL_m^3 / 1e6

scope.basis: a scoped sanity convention over the two numbers a design always commits; it is trivially true for every real organism and exists only to exercise the registry -> surfaces loop end to end
assumed: the committed SL_m and mass_kg describe the same body
scope.note: TEST-LOOP-ONLY. This law is a loop test, not a scientific claim. It is deliberately trivially true: a bound a million times looser than water density cannot eliminate any design a person would propose. It exists so that lean/registry/LIVE-LOOP-DEMO.md can show one law reaching all eight surfaces and changing a design's verdict, with no code edited. Retire it once the demonstration is recorded.

browser_check.note: TEST-LOOP-ONLY: a deliberately trivially true density sanity bound, a million times looser than water. It is here to prove the registry -> evaluator -> Studio -> optimizer -> validation loop closes without a code edit; it rules out nothing a person would propose.

non_vacuity_witness.statement: a 0.04 m, 0.0009 kg zebrafish larva satisfies it with 17 orders of magnitude to spare (0.0009 <= 1e6 x 0.04^3 = 64), so the bound is not vacuous and not binding

origin.from: authored for lean/registry/LIVE-LOOP-DEMO.md; candidate is the automatic ceiling and no human approval is claimed
